value.name: recount mother's declining dependence
value.description: A speaker describes how the mother could not be alone at night and increasingly depended on family help over the past year.
evidence: "In the last year she could not be alone in the house at night. You came home for two weeks in May and you stayed seven months. You slept in the sewing room. You drove her to her appointments. You bathed her in August when she could not lift her arms. Daniel came for Sundays."
value.time_hint: in the last year; May; seven months; August; Sundays

value.name: Daniel defends his work obligations
value.description: Daniel responds that he works, pushing back against the implication that he should have been more present.

value.name: speaker denies blaming Daniel
value.description: The speaker insists they are not blaming Daniel and are only stating who was present for the mother.
evidence: "I am not blaming you. I am telling her what her mother meant."

value.name: Asha pauses the room
value.description: Asha raises a hand to take control of the conversation and calm the room.
evidence: "Asha lifted a hand, gently, and the room paused for her."

value.name: Asha orders codicil investigation
value.description: Asha states that the estate has a witness account of a codicil but not the document itself, and she will investigate whether it exists.
evidence: "Here is where we are. We have a witness account of a codicil. We do not have the codicil. Before this estate moves any further, I am going to find out whether that document exists."

value.name: Asha assigns follow-up contacts
value.description: Asha says she will contact the successor firm and the witness to verify the codicil.
evidence: "I will contact Pinsky's successor firm. I will contact the witness, Mrs. Adelman."

value.name: Asha freezes house listing
value.description: Asha orders that the house not be listed until the codicil question is resolved.
evidence: "In the meantime, no one is listing this house."
"Daniel, no one is listing this house."

value.name: Asha explains sale risk
value.description: Asha explains that selling the house before confirming the codicil could create an irreversible mistake for the estate.
evidence: "Not because I am taking a side. Because if a codicil surfaces after a sale that the codicil would have prevented, we have undone something we cannot redo. The estate can absorb two weeks. It cannot absorb that."

value.name: Daniel reluctantly accepts delay
value.description: Daniel restrains his anger and agrees to a two-week delay, though he repeats the limit skeptically.
evidence: "Daniel breathed out slowly through his nose. He was, she had to admit, very good at not exploding. He nodded once, tightly. "Two weeks," he said."
"Two weeks," he said again, as if saying it could make it so.

value.name: Asha leaves the house
value.description: Asha departs the house in the afternoon after the tense discussion.
evidence: "When she left the house that afternoon"

value.name: Rosa escorts Asha to the door
value.description: Rosa walks Asha to the door as the rain has stopped and the street smells of wet brick.
evidence: "Rosa walked her to the door. The rain had stopped. The street smelled of wet brick."

value.name: Rosa begins private conversation
value.description: At the doorway, Rosa quietly starts speaking to Asha, suggesting a confidential or important exchange is about to follow.
